description: We're Siang Woo and Shi Wei: two builders who share the initials SW, so our team is (SW)², SW squared. Siang Woo led the product, the body map and the astronaut vector that links the tabs. Shi Wei built the Cardio, Sleep, Immune and Bone tabs and their NASA data replays.
summary:
MicroG Sentinel is an offline health check-in app for astronauts on long missions. On the ISS, crew members speak privately with their flight surgeon about once a week; on the way to Mars, a message takes up to 20 minutes each way. Between those calls, astronauts need a fast way to notice change in their own body and to know when it cannot wait.

The home screen is a 3D body map. Tapping a region opens a tab for one NASA spaceflight health risk: cardio, sleep, immune, bone, balance, gut microbiome, eyes (SANS), nutrition and mood. Each tab has its own quick input, compares results with that person's own baseline, and includes a read-only replay of a real NASA study. An "astronaut vector" of traits, baselines and recent exposures links the tabs: a shellfish meal logged in Food raises the hives pattern in Immune for a crew member with a shellfish allergy, with every reason listed.

Results are pattern matches, never diagnoses. Any red-flag answer hides the score and tells the astronaut to contact the flight surgeon now.
details:
LINKS

Live app: https://micro-g-sentinel.vercel.app/

Code and walkthrough: https://github.com/S-W-Leong/microG-sentinel

Demo video: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/S-W-Leong/microG-sentinel@1acaed1ec9c9/docs/demo/MicroG-Sentinel-demo.mp4

WHAT IT DOES

MicroG Sentinel turns NASA's five hazards of human spaceflight into a body map. Altered gravity maps to Cardio, Bone, Balance and SANS (eyes); isolation and confinement to Sleep and Mood; the hostile, closed environment to Immune, Microbiome and Food. Radiation appears as a mission dose card against NASA's 600 mSv career limit, and distance from Earth is why every red flag hands off to the flight surgeon.

HOW IT WORKS

- Body map: a 3D astronaut (three.js) with region cards showing each tab's latest result.

- Risk tabs: each has its own input and display, such as a night-by-night sleep log, five confirmed hives signs with an optional skin photo for the record, meal logging against daily targets, or daily mood sliders. Results are compared with the crew member's own baseline or a reference pattern.

- Astronaut vector: a shared record of each crew member's traits (allergies, chronotype, motion-sickness history), baselines and last-24-hour exposures. Tabs publish small signals to it and read each other's, so results are personalised and every adjustment is shown as a reason.

- Escalation: red-flag questions in each tab. Any "yes" replaces the score with "Contact the flight surgeon now". Unclear or persistent changes are marked "Raise at your next private medical conference".

- Crew profile: shows the vector and which tab affected which result.

- A simulated mission (day 100, three crew members with different stories) fills the app so the links between tabs can be demonstrated.

REAL NASA DATA IN EVERY TAB

Each tab has a read-only "NASA replay", kept separate from crew data:

Cardio: MR080G bed-rest exercise tests. Sleep: BRSMAct wrist actigraphy. Immune: OSD-575 Inspiration4 cytokine panel. Bone: MR035G DXA scans. Microbiome: OSD-574 Inspiration4 skin microbiome. SANS: OSD-679 head-down-tilt eye study (rats; human eye scans need a data request). Balance: UTMB Functional Mobility Test. Mood: AD ASTRA (CFT70) bed-rest mood ratings. Food: MR016G dietary intake.

Data comes from the NASA Life Sciences Data Archive and the Open Science Data Repository, with raw files and curation scripts kept for traceability. Established screening scores (for example UAS7, PSQI, PHQ-9, MUST) are worded as "pattern for follow-up", and we state that their thresholds come from Earth populations.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Astronauts get a quick daily check that is personal to them, works with no connection, and makes clear when to call for help. Flight surgeons get structured observations instead of memory at the weekly call. The design suits Moon and Mars missions, where live help can be minutes away.

TOOLS

TypeScript, React 19 and Vite; three.js for the 3D body map; Observable Plot for charts; Python for NASA data curation; Vitest and Playwright for tests (490 unit tests). No backend: the app runs fully offline in the browser.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

Instead of one dashboard, each risk gets the input and chart that fit it, tied together by a per-person vector, so one log changes another result with the reason shown. Every tab pairs the crew check-in with real NASA research data.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Safety (no diagnosis, treatment advice or "cleared" wording), honesty about data (simulated crew data always labelled, real NASA data kept separate, missing values never treated as zero), minimal text for crew use, accessibility (status never shown by colour alone; works at 320 px wide), offline use and privacy (health data stays on the device).
